caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1644 of 2004
lawyer:
AKM Zahirul Hoque, Advocate, instructed by Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioner. 
Not represented—The Respondents.
parties:
Rustum Ali ----- Petitioners 
Vs.
Hanufa Begum and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment dated September 1, 2004 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4199 of 2001 making absolute the Rule obtained against the judgment and order dated April 12, 2001 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, (now Joint District Judge) Patuakhali in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 51 of 2000 allowing the same upon setting aside the judgment and order dated May 29, 2000 of the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Bauphal, Patuakhali in Miscellaneous Case No. 47 of 1994 allowing the prayer for pre-emption sought under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in respect of the sale that took place on 7-3-1993. 

 2. The pre-emptor filed the Miscellaneous case claiming to be the co-sharer by inheritance as well as by purchase of SA Khatian Nos. 684 and 685. It was stated by pre-emptor that the opposite party No. 2 (in the Miscellaneous case) sold 9.5 decimals of land on March 7, 1993 to the opposite party No. 1 (in the Miscellaneous case), that the said opposite party No. 1 is a stranger purchaser in the holding, that no notice of the transfer was served on the petitioner i.e. pre-emptor, that the purchaser i.e. the preemptee (opposite party No. 1 in the Miscellaneous case) did not go into possession of the land so purchased by him, that pre-emptor came to know about the transfer on 31st Ashar, 1401 BS corresponding to July 15, 1994 on which date pre-emptee disclosed about the purchase made by him, that pre-emptor became definite about the transfer upon obtaining certified copy of the kabala on August 23, 1994, that the pre-emptor is entitled to claim the pre-emption since he is only possessing 2 acres of land. 

 3. The prayer for pre-emption was opposed by filing written statement stating, inter alia that the Miscellaneous case was bad for defect of party and the preemptee is not a stranger purchaser in the holding, that by the purchase in 1987 and by exchange in 1995 preemptee acquired 13.75 decimals of land in SA Khatian No. 684 and 16.50 decimals in SA Khatian No. 685, that prior to selling of the land to him the seller offered the land to the pre-emptor but he refused to purchase because of not having money to purchase the land, that preemptor's claim of knowing about the sale for the first time on July 15, 1994 is not correct and the said claim is not true, that transfer took place within the knowledge of the pre-emptor, that preemptee has made development costing Taka 25,000, that preemptee has become co-sharer on the death of Zohur Jan Bibi on December 11, 1995 and, as such, the preemptee is the co-sharer of the holding. 

 5. The preemptee went on appeal. The appellate Court allowed the appeal upon setting aside the judgment and order of the trial Court on the finding that evidence of PW 1 is inconsistent with the averment made in the petition upon which the Miscellaneous case was registered, that PW 2 has not supported the case of the petitioner since he has not disclosed where preemptee stated to him about the purchase sought to be pre-empted, that from the evidence led by the pre-emptor his case of initial knowledge has not been established. The appellate Court held that the preemptee since his purchase possessed the land and as the pre-emptor failed to establish his initial date of knowledge it can be presumed that he had knowledge of sale from the very date of transfer and, as such, right of pre-emption having had accrued on 7-3-1993 i.e. the date of execution and presentation of the kabala for registration and subsequently on 18-5-1993 the date on which kabala was registered under section 60 of the Registration, Act and as the case was filed on 31-8-1994 after the expiry of prescribed period of 4 months in section 96 (1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and consequent thereupon as the Miscellaneous case was filed beyond the period of limitation, the said Miscellaneous case was barred by limitation and, as such, was not maintainable and ought to have been dismissed by the trial Court on the ground of limitation. 

 7. We have heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner and perused the materials in the petition for leave to appeal. It is seen from the materials on record that pre-emptor was a non-notified co-sharer and it was his claim that he came to know about the sale that took place on 7-3-1993 for the first time on 15-7-1994 and thereupon had the definite knowledge upon obtaining certified copy on 23-8-1994 and then filed the suit on 31-8-1994. The preemptor in support of his initial knowledge examining himself as PW 1 and PW 2. The preemptee alone deposed in the case. In that state of the matter we are of the view that preemptee failed to disprove the case of the pre-emptor about the initial knowledge of the transfer by examining independent witness. 

 8. In the afore state of the matter we are of the view the High Court Division has not committed any error in setting aside the judgment of the lower appellate Court reversing the judgment and order of the trial Court allowing the prayer for pre-emption.
